resources.string: Prefix not recognised – check the callsign

The DXCC country, zones and local time work offline (cty.csv database). Station locator: from PSK Reporter (digital modes in the last 24 h), APRS-IS (last 2 h), your log, QRZCQ and HamQTH (logins in Settings) or HamDB (USA, Canada, Germany, Czechia, Australia). Without a locator no distance is shown.
Callsign not found in the available databases.
We have no locator data for this station – distance and bearing are unavailable.
Ask the other station for their locator. If they use FT8/FT4, the locator may appear in PSK Reporter.
Your position is unknown – turn on location or enter a locator in “Locator and bearing”.
Basic time zone of the country, without daylight saving time; large countries have several zones.
Optional: a HamQTH login in Settings → Service accounts adds the locator and QSL information (bureau, LoTW, eQSL).
You have no QSOs with this callsign yet.
Working out the country from your position… If this takes long (no internet), choose a country from the list.
You are in Poland – you operate under your own callsign.
This country does not apply CEPT recommendation T/R 61-01.
To transmit you need a permit from the local authority or a licence under a bilateral agreement. Check the regulations before you travel.
CEPT country – a class 1 (CEPT) licence lets you operate during a short stay without an additional permit.
Non-CEPT country applying T/R 61-01 – the CEPT licence is recognised.
The prefix depends on the province (VE1–VE9, VO1, VO2, VY0–VY2) – turn on location to pick it.
In CW: prefix/callsign with a slash; in phone: “prefix stroke callsign”.

string-array.item: The CEPT licence covers temporary stays only; for a longer stay you need a local licence.
Carry your licence (the CEPT document) – you must show it on request.
The rules of the host country apply: bands, power and local restrictions.
A guest station cannot claim protection from interference.

resources.string: Note: a different band plan than in Poland (e.g. 40 m up to 7.300 in R2).
